summary: A complete target-level planning pass for symplectic K-theory of Z, CM generation, and its finite, p-adic and locally split universal Galois extensions. 42 targets extend ArithmeticKTheory while importing the generic spectral, Hermitian, CM, moduli and étale-realization owners. The characteristic-number application uses strict prime bounds and the repaired Hurewicz range. Explicit supplier requests and three gaps keep planned coverage distinct from a closed proof plan.

nodes.title: Universal cyclic Bott class
nodes.statement: For odd q, the Bockstein followed by Hurewicz identifies π₂(Σ∞₊B(Z/q);Z/q) with H₁(B(Z/q);Z)=Z/q. Let β_q correspond to 1. Its image in connective complex K-theory under the tautological character is the Bott generator in degree two. Raising the character to a∈(Z/q)× sends β_q to aβ_q. For q>4 its powers generate a split polynomial subalgebra (Z/q)[β_q] in stable homotopy; at q=3 only iterated Bott maps from the supplier contract are used.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime, n≥1 and q=p^n; coefficients Λ_q=Z/q.
ζ_q=exp(2πi/q); twists M(j)=μ_q(C)^{⊗j} carry the left action χ_cyc^j; negative powers mean dual tensor powers.

sources.match: Lemma 2.3 identifies the Bockstein-normalized cyclic class and its character image; the polynomial assertion uses the odd Moore multiplication exception stated immediately before it.

proofSteps: Compute the low-degree stable-homotopy/Bockstein sequence using the absence of odd-primary stable stems in degrees one and two.
Compare the tautological cyclic representation with the topological Bott class, and use its powers for the retraction.
Use H.6’s nonassociative exception at q=3 rather than treating all odd Moore spectra as associative rings.
acceptance: For q=5 and a=2, the degree-two class maps to twice the generator; the unit in degree zero is retained because suspension is unreduced.
At q=3 no assertion of a homotopy-associative Moore multiplication is admitted.

nodes.title: Picard-to-K map
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R, specialize the imported Picard-groupoid construction to invertible R-modules, isomorphisms, and tensor product. Its components are Mathlib’s CommRing.Pic R and its unit automorphisms are R×. The tensor functor to projective modules gives a multiplicative map Σ∞₊|Pic(R)|→K(R), using K.7’s coherent tensor product separately from additive group completion. For a Dedekind domain, representatives by fractional ideals give morphisms from I to J by a∈Frac(R)× satisfying aI=J; these are not restricted to R×.

sources.match: Definition 2.6 gives the invertible-module groupoid and its tensor-induced K-map. The fractional-ideal presentation is corrected by E19; Appendix A supplies the additive machine, with multiplicative coherence requested separately.

proofSteps: Use the existing invertible-module carrier and its tensor equivalences, with Core morphisms.
Import the generic additive spectrum adjunction and the distinct coherent tensor-product comparison.
Verify the automorphism and component comparisons before forming the induced map.
acceptance: Check that a representative decomposition by Pic(R) is natural as a module comparison only after choices, without asserting a canonical product decomposition of ring spectra.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic Picard classes
nodes.statement: Put K_q=Q(ζ_q), O_q=Z[ζ_q] and O′_q=O_q[1/p]. For k≥1 the map (Pic(O_q)/q)⊗μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}→K_{4k−2}(O_q;Z/q)^(+) sending [L]⊗ζ_q^{⊗(2k−1)} to β(ζ_q)^{2k−1}([L]−1) is an isomorphism onto the positive eigensummand. For all k∈Z the same formula in Bott-inverted K-theory is an isomorphism. Inverting p does not change this Picard group because the unique prime over p is principal. These identifications are Galois-equivariant; ψ⁻¹ acts by +1 on the target.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime, n≥1 and q=p^n; coefficients Λ_q=Z/q.
ζ_q=exp(2πi/q); twists M(j)=μ_q(C)^{⊗j} carry the left action χ_cyc^j; negative powers mean dual tensor powers.

sources.match: Corollary 2.12 identifies reduced ideal classes times an odd Bott power with the positive even group; Proposition 2.9 supplies the connective comparison ranges, retaining degree one as an exception.

proofSteps: Use the N.6 even-degree cohomology and comparison contract, including its exceptional degree-one boundary.
Identify the H² term by the Kummer exact sequence and vanishing of the relevant Brauer group for O′_q.
Compare the Kummer edge with the Picard-to-K map and Bott multiplication; retain conjugation and cyclotomic weights.
acceptance: For the trivial ideal L=O_q, [L]−1 maps to zero.
For k=1 the formula lies in K₂ and uses one Bott factor, not β².

nodes.title: Cyclotomic transfer descent
nodes.statement: For every k∈Z, transfer induces an isomorphism (K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(O′_q;Z/q)^(+))_{Gal(K_q/Q)}≅K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(Z[1/p];Z/q)^(+). There is the parallel isomorphism in degree 4k for the negative eigensummand. In the positive comparison range these identify ordinary groups over O_q and Z. Transfer commutes with the duality involution here after accounting for the inverse different, whose ideal class is principal.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime, n≥1 and q=p^n; coefficients Λ_q=Z/q.
ζ_q=exp(2πi/q); twists M(j)=μ_q(C)^{⊗j} carry the left action χ_cyc^j; negative powers mean dual tensor powers.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.15 and proof, pp. 247–248; Lemmas 2.11 and 2.14, pp. 243–247
sources.match: Proposition 2.15 proves the coinvariant transfer isomorphism from the two étale tables. Its duality discussion uses the trace-dual inverse different, whose principal class removes the twist in this case.

proofSteps: Use Poitou–Tate to dualize the transfer into restriction on compactly supported H¹.
Apply the relative homological Hochschild–Serre edge; the odd twist and central conjugation eliminate the outer terms.
Compare duality with transfer using the trace-dual line and its principal ideal class.
acceptance: The source is coinvariants, not invariants; the degree-4k companion uses the negative sign.
No ordinary degree-one Bott comparison is inferred.

nodes.title: Artin–Bott transfer square
nodes.statement: Let H_q/K_q be the maximal everywhere-unramified abelian p-extension inside C, and G_q=Gal(H_q/Q). Arithmetic Artin reciprocity identifies Pic(O_q)⊗Z_p with Gal(H_q/K_q). For every k∈Z and M_q=μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}, the Artin/Bott identifications and transfer give a commuting square from H₁(Gal(H_q/K_q);M_q) to K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(O_q;Z/q)^(+) and from H₁(G_q;M_q) to K^{(β)}_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q)^(+). Its vertical arrows are group-homology pushforward and K-transfer. The bottom map is an isomorphism; H₁(G_q;M_q)≅H₁(G_q,⟨c⟩;M_q), where c is complex conjugation.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime, n≥1 and q=p^n; coefficients Λ_q=Z/q.
ζ_q=exp(2πi/q); twists M(j)=μ_q(C)^{⊗j} carry the left action χ_cyc^j; negative powers mean dual tensor powers.

sources.match: Proposition 2.17 compares the Artin class-group map and K-transfer. Section 7.2 uses the odd conjugation action to identify the absolute kernel with the relative group for ⟨c⟩.

proofSteps: Compare Picard classes with the unramified p-class field using arithmetic Frobenius consistently.
The homological Hochschild–Serre sequence identifies H₁(G_q;M_q) with twisted class-group coinvariants: the quotient’s homology with the odd twist vanishes by central c.
Use the vanishing of H₀ and H₁ of ⟨c⟩ on M_q, since c acts by −1 and 2 is a unit.
acceptance: Replacing arithmetic reciprocity by its inverse requires changing both horizontal maps.
For a regular prime with trivial p-class groups the bottom H₁ and arithmetic kernel are zero.

nodes.title: Betti and Hodge maps
nodes.statement: Use H.4’s symplectic group completion of finite free unimodular alternating Z-modules, with basepoint component BSp∞(Z)⁺, as KSp(Z). Define c_B:KSp(Z)→K(Z) by forgetting the form. Define c_H:KSp(Z)→ku using Sp(Z)→Sp(R)^top←U^top and the homotopy equivalence on the right. On topological complex K-theory ψ⁻¹ is complex conjugation. Hermitian forms are linear in their first variable; the Hodge complex structure is fixed by the condition that its imaginary Hermitian pairing equals the supplied alternating form.

sources.match: Definitions 3.1 and 3.3 use forgetting the form and the topological symplectic-to-unitary equivalence. The linear-first imaginary-part convention requires the recorded sign adapter to the native compatible structure.

proofSteps: Import the KSp carrier and its plus/group-completion equivalence; apply forgetful and scalar-extension functors.
Use the compatible-complex-structure space and its contractibility to identify topological symplectic and unitary classifying spaces.
Compare the Hodge structure sign with the existing compatible-form theorem; do not choose a discontinuous arbitrary inverse.
acceptance: The standard rank-two symplectic lattice maps to 2 in K₀(Z) and 1 in π₀ku.
The two maps are maps of spectra before any Galois action is imposed; c_B is not declared Galois-equivariant on all KSp groups.

nodes.title: Bott-inverted symplectic K-theory
nodes.statement: For q=p^n choose the compatible Adams v₁ self-map on a mod-q Moore spectrum of degree m=2p^{n−1}(p−1) supplied by H.6, and let T_q be its telescope. Put KSp^{(β)}(Z;Z/q)=KSp(Z)∧T_q, with the associated ordinary-to-periodic map. Define the Z_p version by the homotopy inverse limit over the coefficient tower. The Betti and Hodge maps extend to K^{(β)} and KU. The q=3 construction uses an iterated self-map, with no associative Moore-ring assumption.

sources.match: Remark 2.8 and §3.6 use v₁ self-maps and compatible periodic spectra, with p-adic groups defined by completion. The iterated mod-3 construction is retained without an associative Moore product.

proofSteps: Import the compatible telescope and change-of-coefficients contract.
Smash with KSp and extend the detection maps through the telescope.
Form the p-adic homotopy limit, retaining the Milnor sequence until finiteness eliminates its derived limit.
acceptance: Finite coefficients admit the stated v₁-periodicity. No fixed-period assertion is made for the inverse-limit Z_p groups.

nodes.title: Hermitian coefficient-line groupoids
nodes.statement: For a CM field E, maximal order O with conjugation, and an invertible O-module ω with semilinear involution ι, let P(O,ω,ι) have invertible O-modules L with a perfect O-linear pairing b:L⊗_O bar L≅ω such that swapping the two factors agrees with ι. Arrows are O-linear isometries. Set P⁺=P(O,O,conjugation) and P⁻=P(O,ω_{O/Z},−conjugation), where the inverse different is the trace-dual line. Tensoring coefficient lines gives P⁺ an action on P⁻. A P⁻ object has a CM type determined by the signs of Im τ(b(x,x)), x≠0. This specializes CM.2’s polarized lattices; it is not another definition of CM lattices.

sources.match: Definitions 4.2–4.4 give perfect coefficient-line pairings, isometries, conjugate tensor factors and the P⁺ action on P⁻. Norm-one units are the automorphisms; μ_q is only the subgroup used for Bott classes.

proofSteps: Reuse invertible modules, conjugate scalar action and the trace-dual inverse-different interface.
Impose perfectness and the coefficient-line swap condition; isometries form the Core groupoid.
Tensor forms and coefficient lines, and compare the skew form with the existing polarized-lattice sign convention.
acceptance: The full automorphism group of an object is the norm-one unit group; μ_q is only a specified subgroup when E=K_q.

nodes.title: Trace polarization and CM realization
nodes.statement: There is a functor ST:P⁻_E→A_g(C) with g=[E:Q]/2. It sends (L,b) to the principally polarized CM abelian variety obtained from the symplectic lattice (L_Z,−Tr_{E/Q}b) and its unique compatible complex structure of type Φ(L,b). The positive Hermitian form is h(x,y)=−2i Σ_{τ∈Φ}τ b(x,y), with Im h=−Tr b. For this linear-first convention, ω(v,J_H v)=−h(v,v); hence the compatible almost-complex structure in Tau Ceti’s convention is −J_H for ω=Im h. Equivalently J_H is compatible with −ω. This sign adapter is required before invoking exists_compatible. The O-action is faithful and its Rosati involution restricts to conjugation. ST identifies P⁻ with the rank-one projective O-homology locus of CM.2’s classification. For a positive Hermitian O-line X, ST(L⊗X)≅ST(L)⊗_O X compatibly with polarization; (O,−1) gives complex conjugation.

sources.match: Section 4.3 constructs the trace polarization and positive Hermitian form for a unique CM type, then applies complex uniformization. The native almost-complex convention reverses J_H; positive-line Serre tensor and the negative unit line have distinct effects.

proofSteps: Check perfection of −Tr b against the inverse different and compare the sign with CM.2’s ξ convention.
Apply the imported polarized Hodge equivalence and CM classification, rather than reproving algebraization.
Use the existing Serre tensor functor and show its polarization agrees with tensoring coefficient lines.
acceptance: For E=Q(i), the lattice rank is two and the resulting abelian variety has dimension one.
An isometry of CM lines induces a polarized O-linear isomorphism; an arbitrary isogeny is not such an arrow.

nodes.title: Split primes with prescribed signs
nodes.statement: For E=K_q and E⁺ its real subfield, any sign function on the real embeddings of E⁺ is realized by t∈O_{E⁺} whose principal ideal is a prime away from p splitting in E, so (t)O_E=x bar x for a prime ideal x of O_E. The narrow Hilbert class field used in the proof is the full narrow class field of E⁺, distinct from the p-Hilbert field H_q.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime, n≥1 and q=p^n; coefficients Λ_q=Z/q.
ζ_q=exp(2πi/q); twists M(j)=μ_q(C)^{⊗j} carry the left action χ_cyc^j; negative powers mean dual tensor powers.

sources.match: Lemma 4.8 applies Chebotarev to the narrow class field of the real subfield and its disjoint CM extension. E2 corrects the real-embedding and rational-prime notation in the printed proof.

proofSteps: Encode the prescribed sign pattern by a narrow ideal class, using the existing narrow class-group/sign exact sequence.
The narrow Hilbert class field is unramified at finite places, whereas E/E⁺ is ramified at the prime above p; hence their intersection is E⁺.
Apply Chebotarev to the desired class and trivial Frobenius in E/E⁺, and choose a generator with the specified signs.
acceptance: For a real field with one embedding, both positive and negative sign patterns must be supported.
The proof refers to embeddings of E⁺ into R, not to nonexistent real embeddings of E.

nodes.title: CM types and ideal differences
nodes.statement: For q odd, every CM type Φ on K_q and every invertible ideal L of O_q admit B₁,B₂∈P⁻_{K_q}, both of type Φ, whose underlying ideal classes satisfy [B₁][B₂]^{−1}=[L][bar L]^{−1}. Thus all types occur, while prescribed anti-conjugate ideal differences can be realized without changing the Hodge type.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime, n≥1 and q=p^n; coefficients Λ_q=Z/q.
ζ_q=exp(2πi/q); twists M(j)=μ_q(C)^{⊗j} carry the left action χ_cyc^j; negative powers mean dual tensor powers.

sources.match: Proposition 4.7 realizes every type and the anti-conjugate ideal ratio. Its split-prime sign correction permits the two representatives to have the same type without fixing each individual ideal class.

proofSteps: Use a purely imaginary generator δ of the inverse different to start with underlying modules O_q and L/bar L.
Apply the prescribed-sign split-prime theorem to correct each polarization sign while keeping their ratio of ideal classes unchanged.
Verify the resulting pairings are perfect and the types equal Φ.
acceptance: For L=O_q the two underlying classes have equal ratio one.
Changing a single conjugate pair in Φ must be realizable without changing the requested ideal ratio.

nodes.title: CM Bott classes
nodes.statement: For (L,b)∈P⁻_{K_q} and k≥1, let z_{L,b}=β_q^{2k−1}[L,b]∈KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q). Here β acts through the specified μ_q subgroup of norm-one automorphisms, the unreduced stable nerve of P⁻, and its trace-form map to KSp. Products are supplied as iterated maps at q=3. Tensoring positive lines acts through this stable construction; a class [L,b] is in degree zero and its Bott translate has degree 4k−2.

sources.match: The maps (5.1)–(5.3) use the specified root-of-unity automorphisms of CM lines to send the universal stable Bott class to KSp. Their degree and coefficient conventions give the exponent 2k−1.

proofSteps: Use μ_q→Aut(L,b) to obtain the cyclic stable source.
Apply the trace-form functor and the additive spectrum adjunction, importing the compatible tensor/module pairing.
Fix Bott powers and coefficient maps before passing between different CM objects.
acceptance: The construction keeps the degree-zero component rather than replacing the stable nerve by reduced homology.

nodes.title: Hodge type character formula
nodes.statement: If Φ⊂(Z/q)× is the type of (L,b), then c_H(β_q^i[L,b])=(Σ_{a∈Φ}a^i)·bott^i in π_{2i}(ku;Z/q). For odd i, the span of these scalars as Φ varies is all Z/q: changing the choice in one conjugate pair changes the sum by ±2a^i, a unit. Consequently c_H:KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q)→Z/q is onto for k≥1, independently of the Betti–Hodge splitting theorem.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime, n≥1 and q=p^n; coefficients Λ_q=Z/q.
ζ_q=exp(2πi/q); twists M(j)=μ_q(C)^{⊗j} carry the left action χ_cyc^j; negative powers mean dual tensor powers.

sources.match: Proposition 5.2 computes the unitary character sum. Switching one conjugate pair changes an odd power sum by a unit, giving the independent surjectivity input for Proposition 3.8.

proofSteps: Decompose the CM Hodge representation into characters indexed by Φ.
Apply the universal Bott character formula to each summand.
Change one conjugate pair and use that 2 and a are units. This proves surjectivity without using Theorem 3.5.
acceptance: For q=5, i=1, changing {1,2} to {−1,2} changes 3 to 1, a unit difference.
For even i conjugate-pair switching has zero difference; the oddness hypothesis is essential.

nodes.title: Betti transfer formula
nodes.statement: For (L,b)∈P⁻_{K_q}, c_B(z_{L,b})=tr_{O_q/Z}(β(ζ_q)^{2k−1}([L]−1)). This depends only on L. The term tr(β^{2k−1}) vanishes because conjugation acts with sign −1 on the odd Bott power whereas transfer lands in the positive eigensummand.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime, n≥1 and q=p^n; coefficients Λ_q=Z/q.
ζ_q=exp(2πi/q); twists M(j)=μ_q(C)^{⊗j} carry the left action χ_cyc^j; negative powers mean dual tensor powers.

sources.match: Diagram (5.7) and Corollary 5.4 identify forgetting the form with K-transfer. Conjugation removes the transferred odd Bott unit term, leaving the reduced ideal class.

proofSteps: Compare the trace-form forgetful functor with restriction of scalars of the underlying O_q-module.
Use Picard-to-K multiplicativity for the ideal factor.
Remove the unit term by conjugation and the invertibility of 2.
acceptance: If L=O_q the Betti image is zero even when its Hodge image is nonzero.
The exponent is 2k−1 throughout, including the Galois difference calculation.

nodes.title: Betti–Hodge splitting theorem
nodes.statement: For i≥0 and q odd, (p_+c_B,p_-c_H):KSp_i(Z;Z/q)≅K_i(Z;Z/q)^(+)⊕π_i(ku;Z/q)^(−), where p_±=(1±ψ⁻¹)/2. In degree 4k−2, k≥1, this is K_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q)⊕Z/q, with the arithmetic term identified with H²_et(Z[1/p];μ_q^{⊗2k}). For i>0 the p-adic groups vanish for i≡0,1 mod4, are K_i(Z;Z_p)⊕Z_p for i≡2 mod4, and are K_i(Z;Z_p) for i≡3 mod4. The direct-sum splitting is an abelian-group assertion, not a Galois-equivariant splitting of the main extension.

nodes.title: Polarized abelian Γ-groupoid
nodes.statement: For a finite pointed set T, define A(T) from principally polarized abelian varieties (A,λ) and a unital ring map φ:Z^T→End(A) whose image is fixed by the Rosati involution defined by λ. Put e=1−e_* and select eA. Arrows are polarized isomorphisms of selected factors commuting with the Z^T-action. For f:T→U, restriction along f*:Z^U→Z^T defines the Γ map. The stack is equivalent to (∐_{g≥0}A_g)^{T\{*}}. This is a ppav specialization of H.4’s Γ construction and the imported ppav moduli stack, not a second generic Γ-space.

Define restriction using f* and compare its selected factor to the product over non-basepoint fibers.
Verify coherence of the product decompositions using the generic Γ-space supplier.

nodes.title: Rigidified ppav simplicial model
nodes.statement: Rigidify the selected factor in A(T) by a projective embedding from the third power of the ample line bundle Δ*L, where L represents the principal polarization correspondence. Its Čech nerve Z(T)_r has r+1 embeddings together with compatible isomorphisms of their ppav objects. It is a specified coproduct of quasi-projective simplicial schemes over Q, graded by dimension vectors. The construction is Γ-functorial through the imported product/rigidification coherence contract; it does not claim the entire unbounded coproduct is one quasi-projective scheme.

nodes.statement: The analytic ppav stack of genus g is H_g//Sp_{2g}(Z), where Siegel space H_g is contractible. Its Betti realization is therefore weakly equivalent to BSp_{2g}(Z). Level N≥4 gives a smooth finite-level atlas; quotient singular complexes are compared by weak equivalences, not literal simplicial isomorphisms. For every finite pointed T, Sing_an Z_C(T)≃N SP_T(Z) naturally as special Γ-spaces; at S⁰ this is ∐_g BSp_{2g}(Z). Applying the existing Segal machine gives KSp(Z).

A special Γ-space has Ω-equivalences in levels n≥1. Its zeroth replacement is group completion: N→Z on genus components, not an equivalence before completion.

nodes.title: Galois action on the symplectic spectrum
nodes.statement: Algebraic conjugation sends a complex ppav with structure map φ to the same underlying scheme with structure map Spec(σ⁻¹)∘φ, and transports its polarization and arrows. This gives a left Aut(C)-action: σ·(τ·A)=(στ)·A. For an odd prime p, use componentwise graded p-completed étale realization of the Q-defined Z(T), with EH.6’s comparison, to obtain a homotopy-coherent Aut(C)-action by spectrum maps on KSp(Z)^∧_p and compatible mod-p^n spectra. For p>3 the vanishing of H₁(A_g;F_p) allows the direct finite-type comparison on each genus. For p=3 first smash each connected component, pointed by a rational ppav, with the simply connected Moore space M(Z/p^n,2), realize this simplicially, compare, then desuspend twice and pass through the tower. Naturality includes the discrete complex-point map. The action is independent, up to the supplied coherent equivalences, of rigidifications and basepoint choices.

nodes.title: Groupoid CM reciprocity formula
nodes.statement: Let E/Q be a Galois CM field with full Hilbert class field H. Choose lifts w_τ:H→C of τ:E→C with w_{cτ}=c w_τ=w_τ c. Transport by σ∈Aut(C) sends type Φ to σΦ. On isometry classes in a fixed-type fiber it is tensoring by a Hermitian line (X,h)∈P⁺_E, depending only on σ and Φ; its archimedean signs need not be positive. In particular σ=c uses (O,−1). Under arithmetic Artin reciprocity its ideal class is represented by ∏_{τ∈Φ} w_{στ}^{−1}σw_τ∈Gal(H/E). Transport commutes naturally with Serre tensor by positive Hermitian lines. For E=K_q the induced stable map sends β_q^j[L,b] to β_q^jF_σ[L,b]; at q=3 interpret powers as the compatible iterated Bott maps. This Bott-linearity is needed before applying reciprocity to the spanning stable CM classes. The formula is in Gal(H/E); H_q denotes the p-subfield only after specialization.

Translate its idelic expression to the chosen conjugation-compatible lifts and the ideal class of X; R12 requests this precise groupoid adapter.
Use the Serre-tensor comparison and the discrete-point equivariance to transport the formula to stable CM classes.

Use positive-line Serre tensor naturality to obtain a module map on stable nerves, then the Bott-linearity of Theorem 6.6(ii); positivity is used for this acting subgroup, not for the translating line X.

For σ=c the line (O,−1) changes Φ to its conjugate. A positive translating line would preserve Φ and contradict this case.

nodes.title: Split extension category
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring Λ, group G, subgroup H and left Λ[G]-module M, let C_Λ(G,H;M) have objects (V,π,s) with π:V→M a surjective G-linear map, trivial G-action on T=ker π, and an H-linear section s:M→V with π∘s=id_M. A morphism f is G-linear, satisfies π′f=π and fs=s′, and may induce any Λ-linear map on kernels. The unsectioned category C_Λ(G;M) remembers only (V,π). The H-split subcategory of that category forgets the chosen section.

Kernels use the inherited representation; demand that each group element act identically there.
Compose the underlying maps; the commuting equations are stable under identity and composition.

nodes.title: Relative bar convention comparison
nodes.statement: For the relative chain complex C_*(G,H;M)=C_*(G;M)/C_*(H;Res M) imported from R02.2, construct its FGV left-coefficient presentation and comparison. It has C₀=0 and H₁ presented by generators [g]⊗m, linear in m, relations [h]⊗m=0 for h∈H and [gg′]⊗m=[g]⊗g′m+[g′]⊗m. Supply an explicit natural chain equivalence with Mathlib’s inhomogeneous-chain convention, whose differential uses inverse actions, before invoking its groupHomology. The canonical α_univ(g,m)=[g]⊗m is a relative 1-cycle class.

nodes.title: Universal relative extension
nodes.statement: There is an equivalence C_Λ(G,H;M)≃(H₁(G,H;M)↓Mod_Λ). Its initial object has underlying module M⊕H₁(G,H;M), projection to M, section m↦(m,0), and action g·(m,t)=(g·m,t+[g]⊗m). If H₀(H;M)=H₁(H;M)=0, forgetting the section is an equivalence to C_Λ(G;M); if only H₀ vanishes, it is an equivalence to its H-split subcategory. In this roadmap these forgetful assertions are used for finite free M and H=⟨c⟩ with c acting by −1 over an odd-primary coefficient ring.

nodes.title: Finite arithmetic Galois action
nodes.statement: For q odd and k≥1, the spectrum action on V_q=KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q) factors through G_q=Gal(H_q/Q). The Hodge map gives an exact G_q-sequence 0→T_q→V_q→M_q→0 with M_q=μ_q^{⊗(2k−1)}, trivial action on T_q, and T_q≅K_{4k−2}(Z;Z/q). The restriction c_H:ker c_B→M_q is an isomorphism and its inverse is the unique ⟨c⟩-equivariant splitting. The Hodge map has weight 2k−1; the Betti map is only conjugation-invariant on V_q.

ζ_q=exp(2πi/q); twists M(j)=μ_q(C)^{⊗j} carry the left action χ_cyc^j; negative powers mean dual tensor powers.

sources.match: Lemma 7.7 uses the spanning CM classes and reciprocity to factor the action, identify the odd Hodge character and fix the arithmetic kernel. Its conjugation splitting is not an equivariant splitting for the whole Galois group. Fixing the p-Hilbert field kills the p-primary ideal class, which suffices modulo q, without forcing the whole ideal class to be principal.

proofSteps: Compute Galois transport on the spanning CM Bott classes using reciprocity and the type character formula.

If σ fixes H_q then its CM type is fixed and its Hermitian tensor line has zero p-primary ideal class. Its ideal class therefore vanishes modulo q, so both detection differences vanish; the full ideal class need not be principal.
Differences between classes of a fixed CM type give fixed arithmetic-kernel generators. Complex conjugation gives the unique splitting because it is −1 on M_q and +1 on T_q.
acceptance: For σ in Gal(C/H_q), every CM generator is fixed in V_q although its geometric ppav representative need not be fixed.
Under the abelian-group coordinates T_q⊕M_q the action may have a nonzero off-diagonal cocycle; it is not declared diagonal.

Equality is in homology modulo boundaries and the ⟨c⟩-chains.

nodes.title: Continuous universal extensions
nodes.statement: Let Γ be a profinite group, H a closed subgroup and M a finite free Z_p-module with continuous action. In C^cts_{Z_p}(Γ,H;M), objects and morphisms are the continuous counterparts of AK2.5 with finitely generated p-complete kernel and middle module and a continuous H-section. Completed relative homology is computed by the completed bar complex, equivalently the inverse system over open normal U and coefficient powers p^n with the induced pair and coefficient coinvariants. For the Γ and G occurring below, finite-coefficient homology is finite and the resulting H₁ is finitely generated; thus its completed universal extension is initial in this category. Surjective finite towers remove the relevant lim¹ obstruction.

nodes.title: p-adic universal extension theorem
nodes.statement: Let H_∞=∪_{n≥1}H_{p^n} and Γ=Gal(H_∞/Q). For k≥1 the spectrum action gives a continuous exact sequence 0→K_{4k−2}(Z;Z_p)→KSp_{4k−2}(Z;Z_p)→Z_p(2k−1)→0. The arithmetic kernel is finite with trivial Γ-action. With its unique conjugation-equivariant section it is initial in C^cts_{Z_p}(Γ,⟨c⟩;Z_p(2k−1)); forgetting that section gives initiality in the unsectioned category of finite-type compact continuous extensions. Its kernel is H₁^cts(Γ,⟨c⟩;Z_p(2k−1)).
hypotheses: p odd prime; k≥1; the finite-type compact coefficient category is fixed as in AK2.7/continuous-extension.

The K-theory coefficient tower has finite groups; its inverse-limit comparison has no lim¹ term. The underlying arithmetic group in this degree is finite.

At a regular prime the kernel vanishes; at an irregular degree with nonzero kernel, a Γ-equivariant section is impossible.

nodes.title: Local splitting and relative homology
nodes.statement: Let Q(p) be the maximal extension of Q unramified outside p and G=Gal(Q(p)/Q). First choose a compatible c-fixed prime above p in H_∞. Extend that place arbitrarily to Q(p), obtaining G_𝔭, and let D_q⊂G_q be its image. The subgroup D_q contains c; the extended place itself is not required to be c-fixed and no assertion c∈G_𝔭 is used. The natural map of pairs (G,G_𝔭)→(G_q,D_q) induces H₁^cts(G,G_𝔭;M_q)≅H₁(G_q,D_q;M_q)≅H₁(G_q,⟨c⟩;M_q). Here D_q≅Gal(K_q/Q) because the principal prime above p splits in H_q/K_q. The KSp extension is uniquely D_q-split and its section has image ker c_B.
hypotheses: p is an odd prime, n≥1 and q=p^n; coefficients Λ_q=Z/q.
ζ_q=exp(2πi/q); twists M(j)=μ_q(C)^{⊗j} carry the left action χ_cyc^j; negative powers mean dual tensor powers.

Its kernel is H₁^cts(G,G_𝔭;Z_p(2k−1)).

nodes.statement: For every integer k, including k≤0, replace the K and KSp groups in the finite, p-adic and local universal extensions by their Bott-inverted versions. At finite q one may move k to a positive integer using a compatible period for both the group and cyclotomic twist. Then pass to the p-adic limit; this passage does not make the Z_p groups periodic.

The symplectic unit made from a rational elliptic curve maps under c_B to twice that unit. Since c_B is an isomorphism in this degree and 2 is invertible, the rational symplectic unit is onto and is Galois-fixed.

nodes.title: Vandiver and conjugation-fixed primes
nodes.statement: For q=p^n, the primes of H_q above p form a torsor under Gal(H_q/K_q). After choosing a c-fixed prime, c acts on this torsor by its action on that p-class group. Thus there is exactly one c-fixed prime precisely when its plus part is zero; under the Iwasawa control interface this is equivalent to Vandiver(p). This assertion concerns c-fixed primes. The entire prime set is a singleton only when the full p-class group vanishes, the regular-prime condition.

nodes.statement: For a connected H-space X of finite type, let I=H_{>0}(X;Z_p) be the augmentation ideal and I_r=H_{>0}(X;Z/p^r). Let β_r:H_j(X;Z/p^r)→H_{j−1}(X;Z_p) be the coefficient Bockstein. Put D=I²+Σ_{r≥1}β_r(I_r²), the Z_p-submodule of integral decomposables, and Q^int_*(X)=I/D. Products in the squares have both factors in strictly positive degree; D is not the indecomposable quotient itself. Coefficients here are ordinary singular homology with Z_p on an integral finite-type X.
